Do Now: Recap Linear Search

A quick recap before today's new instructions, plus one real exam question to preview today's new syntax.

The array Values = [8, 15, 3, 21] is already stored

1  INPUT SearchValue
2  Found <- FALSE
3  FOR Index <- 1 TO 4
4    IF Values[Index] = SearchValue THEN
5      Found <- TRUE
6    ENDIF
7  NEXT Index
8  IF Found = TRUE THEN
9    OUTPUT "Found"
10  ELSE
11    OUTPUT "Not Found"
12  ENDIF

steps.label: Computational Thinking: Breaking Problems Down
steps.content:
Computational Thinking: Breaking Problems Down

Before writing any pseudocode, a computer scientist thinks about the problem itself. Three ideas do most of that work.

  • Algorithmic Thinking means breaking a solution down into a clear sequence of steps.
  • Decomposition means breaking down a larger problem into smaller, more manageable problems.
  • Abstraction means removing unnecessary information so that the important parts of a problem can be focused on.

Today's algorithms combine Sequence, Selection and Iteration. Before writing one: decompose the task into smaller pieces, abstract away anything that doesn't matter, then use algorithmic thinking to put the remaining steps in a clear order.

steps.label: Iteration: Two Kinds of Loop
steps.content:
Iteration: Two Kinds of Loop

You have already used FOR inside a search. Today it gets a name: iteration, repeating a set of instructions.

  • A FOR loop is count-controlled: it runs an exact number of times, known before the loop starts. It ends with NEXT.
  • A WHILE loop is condition-controlled: it keeps running for as long as a condition is TRUE, and the number of passes is not known in advance. It ends with ENDWHILE.
  • From today, every new variable needs a DECLARE line before it is used, stating its name and type: DECLARE Count : INTEGER.
  • Choose FOR when you know exactly how many times to repeat. Choose WHILE when you are repeating until something becomes true, and you cannot know in advance when that will happen.

items.prompt: Two types of pseudocode statements used for iteration are
options: FOR ... NEXT and WHILE ... DO ... ENDWHILE
items.explain: FOR...NEXT and WHILE...DO...ENDWHILE are both iteration (looping) constructs. IF and CASE are selection constructs, not iteration.

items.prompt: A standard method of solution used for adding together a set of values during iteration is
items.explain: Totalling means adding values together as the loop runs, the running-total pattern you just traced. Counting increments by 1 regardless of value; searching and sorting are unrelated patterns.

steps.label: Write Iteration and Selection Together

Write Iteration and Selection Together

The task is to test five scores, one at a time, outputting Pass or Fail for each.

steps.label: Write It Yourself
steps.content:
Write It Yourself

Use the same structure you just learned, but write it yourself this time.

Task

Five test scores will be entered, one at a time. Write pseudocode that:

  • declares the variables it needs
  • uses a FOR loop to receive a Score five times
  • outputs "Pass" if Score is 50 or more, otherwise "Fail"

Remember

  • DECLARE every variable before it is used.
  • Five scores means FOR Count <- 1 TO 5.
  • INPUT and the whole IF/ELSE go inside the loop, they must run on every pass.

steps.label: Checked Practice: Trace a WHILE Loop
steps.content:
Checked Practice: Trace a WHILE Loop

This time you are reading, not writing. Trace it carefully, line by line.

1  DECLARE Stock : INTEGER
2  Stock <- 3
3  WHILE Stock > 0
4    IF Stock = 1 THEN
5      OUTPUT "Last one!"
6    ELSE
7      OUTPUT "In stock"
8    ENDIF
9    Stock <- Stock - 1
10  ENDWHILE

Questions

Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Check Your Understanding
steps.content:
Check Your Understanding

Questions to ask around the room:

  • What is the difference between count-controlled and condition-controlled iteration?
  • Why must every new variable be declared before it is used?
  • Give an example of Decomposition from today's Farmer tutorials.
  • Why might a WHILE loop never stop, but a FOR loop always will?
  • What does it mean to combine Iteration and Selection in one algorithm?

steps.label: Plenary: Question 1
steps.content:
Plenary

Use everything from today. Try this on your own before checking your answer.

Task

Four temperatures will be entered, one at a time. Write pseudocode that:

  • declares the variables it needs
  • uses a FOR loop to receive a Temperature four times
  • outputs "Warm" if Temperature is 20 or more, otherwise "Cool"

Remember

  • Four temperatures means FOR Count <- 1 TO 4.
  • DECLARE every variable before it is used.

steps.label: Plenary: Question 2
steps.content:
Plenary

Harder than Question 1: this time you don't know in advance how many attempts it will take.

Task

A programmer wants to keep asking for a Password until the user types PASS1234 correctly. Write pseudocode that:

  • declares the variables it needs
  • uses a WHILE loop to keep asking for Password until it equals "PASS1234"
  • then outputs "Access Granted"

Remember

  • You cannot know in advance how many attempts it will take, so this needs WHILE, not FOR.
  • INPUT a first attempt before the loop starts, then INPUT again inside the loop, or it could run forever.

y8l5_do_now.feedback: The loop counts from 1 to 4, so line 4 runs once for every position.
Values[3] is 3, which matches SearchValue, so Found becomes TRUE and the output is "Found".
Both variables hold a whole number, so both need DECLARE ... : INTEGER (as two lines, or one combined DECLARE Seconds, Minutes : INTEGER).

y8l5_ct_check.feedback: Splitting one large task into smaller named tasks is Decomposition.
Removing detail that doesn't matter (real distances) to keep only what's useful (station order) is Abstraction.
Putting steps into a clear, ordered sequence is Algorithmic Thinking.

y8l5_practice.feedback: Stock starts at 3 and the loop runs while Stock > 0, so it runs for Stock = 3, 2 and 1: three passes.
On the final pass Stock = 1, so line 4's IF is true and line 5 outputs "Last one!".
After the third pass Stock <- Stock - 1 makes Stock 0, and WHILE Stock > 0 is now false, so the loop ends.
